name: La Once Mil
description: Taquería named for the 11000 postal code of Lomas de Chapultepec. The trompo carries Black Angus picaña, ribeye and A5 wagyu, alongside pork belly and truffle options. It earned a Michelin star in the 2026 Mexico guide, the first for a taquería after El Califa de León lost its star.
special_quality: The only Michelin-starred taquería in the city, with wagyu on the trompo.
google_maps_query: La Once Mil, Lomas, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Maizajo
description: Taquería, restaurant and tortillería built around house-nixtamalized heirloom corn. Thin grilled ribeye and a potato-and-cheese taco are the draws, with bright salsas. Lines are long and it has been in the Michelin guide since 2024.
special_quality: Heirloom-corn tortillas milled in-house make the taco about the masa first.

name: Taquería Selene
description: Family-run trompo taquería said to date to 1964. Known for pastor with a high meat-to-cheese ratio and crisp edges, and for the gringa and beef-rib taco. Often named the best pastor in the city, though some visitors find it good rather than transcendent.
special_quality: Frequently called the city's best al pastor, with a notably crisp, meat-heavy gringa.
